record.reason: The primary abstract describes evolutionary-scale language modeling of protein sequences: training on 86 billion amino acids across 250 million protein sequences to learn biological representations and predict protein properties such as mutational effects and structure. Its subject is biological protein modeling, not natural-language LLM inference/serving or inference-time compression/efficiency. A model being called a language model is insufficient for the stated scope.
record.title: Biological structure and function emerge from scaling unsupervised learning to 250 million protein sequences
